purpose: A narrow, pre-outcome evidence supplement for an independent future A1 curator. It supplies carrier identity and two separately sourced mechanism readings. It is not an A1 receipt, an H1/H2 package, a peer panel, an outcome, a settlement, a method result, a CJO, a valuation, a report, or an investment permission.
package_boundary: This is not an amendment to TURTLE_COMPARATIVE_ACTION_SCREEN_STATIC_PDF_PACKAGE_V2. Its annual-report sources remain outside that action-screen package's low-cost discovery scope and gain no admission status from this supplement.

candidate_binding.cutoff_rule: Every listed static source has a CNInfo finalpage date strictly before the cutoff. CNInfo metadata was used only to enumerate the source identity and date; page facts are from the named static PDFs.

separate_mechanism_evidence.bounded_inference: The issuer itself identifies market and supply-demand drivers that can move operating conditions independently of an internal-supply change. This is the strongest pre-outcome rival reading, not proof that the rival explains any later observation.

limits_and_required_next_gate: The two separate mechanism pages are from a cutoff-before annual report and establish operating context only. They do not supply a Dushan-project measurement, a customer response field, a peer, a control, a counterfactual, or an outcome contract.

This supplement deliberately does not create an A1 candidate receipt. A later independent A1 curator must independently satisfy the A1 schema, including its timestamped source-availability rule, rather than treating date-only metadata in this supplement as an A1 timing grant.
No post-cutoff material, outcome, price, return, valuation, R-103, forecast, CJO, report, H1/H2 stop receipt, peer result, or settlement was accessed in creating this supplement.

The next legal consumer may review this package together with the original C-ACT-003 screen to decide whether an independent timestamp-qualified A1 receipt is possible; it must stop rather than substitute consolidated performance for a same-boundary metric.
